mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to decline, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the labor force participation rate (implied by UNRATE) suggests weak labor market recovery, which typically precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates slower growth.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in 70% of similar labor weakness regimes (out-of-sample cross-section).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, which is associated with higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns as the market anticipates stronger growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous 2 months AND INDPRO < previous 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns under similar imbalances are not statistically superior to a baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend for 4 consecutive months predicts supply-side weakness, which typically results in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as the market discounts future earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in 60% of historical supply contractions (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 2% triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative during similar inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% without a corresponding rise in labor force participation suggests a tight labor market, which can precede short-term negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as the market anticipates wage growth risks.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not persistently negative in similar tight labor regimes (rolling 30-day window).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer demand (HOUST) and business demand (RSAFS) above trend levels indicates a dual-demand expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns as the market expects sustained growth.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not superior to a single-demand proxy (multivariate IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the RSAFS (reserves) series suggests banks are accumulating liquidity, interpreted as a prelude to a future rate hike; this typically results in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative during analogous liquidity buildups (out-of-sample).
